inspection: static published SDK seam research, not execution or live support qualification

sources.observation: Both inspected SSO/device client constructors set user-wallet; no actual session was read.
Public types expose sign-only wire return and per-call presign callback; callback context contains networkId and walletId.

signTransaction selects shared signing with includeSubmissionConfig false and returns rawTransaction. Its KMS sign request omits submissionConfig and X-Rpc-Method is signTransaction. User-wallet preparation still receives network-derived submissionConfig with that method header.
sources.presign_timing: after getTransactionForSigning/prepare and before KMS signing; callback applies only if the prepared value is a string
sources.postsign_interception_in_sign_and_send: not exposed; final signed wire comes back after the KMS submission-enabled request

selected_excerpts.excerpt: const result = await this.performTransactionSigning(params, false, params.presignTransaction);

sources.observation: Its signTransaction method delegates to client.signTransaction and parses the returned raw wire; it does not delegate to signAndSendTransaction in that method. This local implementation is not evidence that remote service authorises the call.

current_official_documentation.observation: Browser SDK docs explicitly state embedded wallets do not support signTransaction/signAllTransactions, and support signAndSendTransaction with a per-call presign callback after Phantom construction/validation. That callback is before the embedded wallet signs; it is not a final signed-wire interception.
current_official_documentation.scope: Current Browser SDK product support statement, not proof of exact CLI account permissions or a resolved SDK dependency graph.

conclusion: A low-level sign-only API exists in inspected client code, but a supported live nonbroadcast path for the intended agent wallet is not established. Stock MCP routes still expose neither this API nor a callback. A presign integration would validate prepared bytes before remote signing, not obtain final signed wire before broadcast.
limitations: No module import/execution, dependencies installed or resolved graph.
No keys, authentication/session reads, RPC, signing or send.
Static absence of KMS submissionConfig is not a live guarantee of remote nonbroadcast or authorisation.
No service capability, byte mutation, interception integration, isolation, independent security or release credit.
No ADR/deployment changes authorised or implemented.
